explanation: In mathematical or quantitative prose the pole fires where a numeral states the value of a quantity computed from other stated quantities: an aggregate over a stated set ('the average/sum/total/difference/product of the four numbers is 34', 'the middle of the three scores', 'the average price of the two shirts is 45 dollars') or a change from a baseline ('raised/increased/rose by 5 dollars', 'grew from 4,000 to 5,200', '10% greater than last month'), peaking on the space token immediately before that numeral, or on the copula, change verb or clause boundary just before it. It stays near zero when the numeral only states a level or a property of a single object ('the price rose to 5 dollars', 'the shirt costs 45 dollars', 'the temperature was 45 degrees', 'page 45', 'the year 1990'), on index words ('the first of the four numbers is 34'), and on numerals in ordinary non-quantitative prose.
